kept.title: Hardcoded Secret used for HMAC benchmarking server
kept.description: The benchmark server uses a hardcoded string 'secretsecretsecret' for JWT signing/verification, which is insecure if used in production.
steps_to_exploit: Locate the benchmark server endpoint
Use the known secret 'secretsecretsecret' to sign arbitrary payloads
Forge valid JWTs with escalated privileges
kept.impact: Full authentication bypass by forging tokens with arbitrary claims.

kept.title: Use of unsafe regex in validator configurations
kept.description: Verifier options allow Regex patterns that are not inherently safe, leading to ReDoS (Regular Expression Denial of Service).
steps_to_exploit: Identify an application using fast-jwt with a configurable regex validator
Submit a crafted, long string designed to trigger exponential backtracking
Observe CPU exhaustion on the server
kept.impact: Denial of service through resource exhaustion.

kept.title: Insecure default cache key builder allows collisions
kept.description: The default cache key builder relies on `hashToken`, which might lead to collisions if not handled correctly across different JWT structures.
steps_to_exploit: Find two distinct tokens that produce the same cache key due to hash collision
Authenticate with the valid token
Inject the malicious token, which the system erroneously treats as the valid cached result
kept.impact: Authentication bypass or privilege escalation due to cache poisoning.

kept.title: Potential timing attacks in signature verification
kept.description: While `timingSafeEqual` is used for HMAC, other signature algorithms rely on `createVerify`, which may not be fully constant-time depending on the underlying Node.js implementation for all elliptic curves.
steps_to_exploit: Collect a large volume of timing data for verification operations
Use statistical analysis to deduce private key bits via timing side-channels

kept.title: Insecure key detection for password protected private keys
kept.description: If a password-protected key is provided without explicitly defining an algorithm, the system attempts to detect the algorithm, potentially leaking sensitive metadata or failing open.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a specially crafted password-protected key
Trigger automatic detection to force the system to perform operations on the unencrypted material in memory
kept.impact: Potential exposure of sensitive key metadata.

kept.title: Missing validation for 'none' algorithm on some endpoints
kept.description: The signer and verifier structures attempt to handle the 'none' algorithm, which is inherently insecure and should be strictly disabled by default.
steps_to_exploit: Modify a token header to set 'alg': 'none'
Remove the signature portion of the JWT
Bypass integrity checks on servers that fail to enforce strict algorithm allow-lists

evidence.quote: const signature = algorithm === 'none' ? '' : createSignature(algorithm, key, input)

code_refs.quote: const signature = algorithm === 'none' ? '' : createSignature(algorithm, key, input)

kept.title: Risk of Prototype Pollution via `mutatePayload`
kept.description: The `mutatePayload` option allows the library to modify the user-provided payload object directly, which can lead to prototype pollution if the input object is attacker-controlled.
steps_to_exploit: Pass a malicious object as payload with `__proto__` properties
Enable `mutatePayload` in the signer options
Observe modifications to the global Object prototype
kept.impact: Remote code execution or significant application state corruption.

kept.title: Lack of strict bounds checking for cache sizes
kept.description: The `createCache` function parses a raw size from user input without sufficient validation, leading to potential memory issues.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a massive integer as the cache size configuration
Trigger cache population until the process exceeds heap limits
kept.impact: Denial of service via memory exhaustion.

evidence.quote: const size = parseInt(rawSize === true ? defaultCacheSize : rawSize, 10)

code_refs.quote: const size = parseInt(rawSize === true ? defaultCacheSize : rawSize, 10)

kept.title: Sensitive information leakage in benchmark logs
kept.description: Benchmarks automatically write logs to disk with file naming based on timestamps, potentially capturing sensitive keys or valid tokens if misconfigured.
steps_to_exploit: Monitor the `benchmarks/logs` directory in a shared or CI environment
Retrieve leaked tokens from stored log files
kept.impact: Exposure of valid authentication tokens and cryptographic material.

kept.title: Unbounded cache duration for error responses
kept.description: Error cache TTL is configurable, and if set improperly or to a very large number, it effectively caches denials.
steps_to_exploit: Submit invalid tokens to fill up the error cache
Force legitimate users into the error-cached state
kept.impact: Denial of service by poisoning the negative cache.

evidence.quote: const ttl = typeof errorCacheTTL === 'function' ? errorCacheTTL(value) : errorCacheTTL

code_refs.quote: const ttl = typeof errorCacheTTL === 'function' ? errorCacheTTL(value) : errorCacheTTL

kept.title: Reliance on `Buffer.from` without explicit encoding checks
kept.description: While there are some base64 checks, relying on Buffer behavior for various string inputs can lead to unexpected handling of malformed input.
steps_to_exploit: Provide non-utf8 encoded binary data in base64 segments
Observe how the library handles the decoding logic
kept.impact: Unexpected logic execution or error-handling bypass.

kept.title: Insecure usage of `process.nextTick` in async callbacks
kept.description: Using `process.nextTick` to wrap callbacks can lead to starvation or bypass synchronous control flow mechanisms.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger multiple async key fetches to exhaust the event loop queue
Cause the application to become unresponsive

kept.title: Blind trust in `JSON.parse` for payload decoding
kept.description: The library parses the payload segment without an explicit schema validator, which is prone to issues if the payload contains unexpected object structures.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a JWT with a massive or complex JSON payload
Exhaust CPU/Memory during the JSON parsing phase

kept.title: Weak validation of `typ` header parameter
kept.description: The header `typ` check performs a loose replacement of 'application/' which might lead to content-type confusion attacks.
steps_to_exploit: Create a JWT with `typ`: 'application/application/jwt'
Observe how the sanitizer allows malformed types through

kept.title: Use of deprecated or weak elliptic curves in key generation
kept.description: The generator for keys includes 'secp256k1' and others which may have varying security profiles compared to modern standards.
steps_to_exploit: Analyze keys generated by the utility for vulnerabilities inherent to specific curves
